clue.text: Cattle food? Nark it!

definitions.meaning: to nark is to act as a police informer, so this asks you to inform on it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nark it!' is British slang for 'Stop it!', but here 'nark' is the informer's verb: inform on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Grazing pasture is what herds eat, and to inform to the police is British slang for telling tales; both senses share the word.

clue.text: What a topping stabilizer !

parts.note: topping means excellent, but also like a spinning top: a spinning wheel device keeping ships and aircraft steady

explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' is old British slang for excellent, but here it means acting like a spinning top.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning wheel that resists tilting is used to keep ships and aircraft stable, and it spins like a child's top.

clue.text: Thames crime for VIP's only

parts.note: an unremarkable person is said to be one who will never set the Thames on fire, so only a VIP could commit that offence

explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'he'll never set the Thames on fire' describes someone ordinary; the Thames is London's river.
explanation.definitionFit: The crime of deliberately setting fire to property; setting the Thames on fire is the idiom for great achievement.

clue.text: Bonded with alloy and iron

parts.note: metal parts joined with a low-melting alloy, melted with a hot electric tool called an iron

explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' reads as a second metal in the bond, but it is the heated tool used to melt the alloy.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal joints are made by melting a tin alloy with a heated iron, so the parts are joined this way.

clue.text: Fire performance

definitions.meaning: to fire a gun is to let it off
the carrying out of a duty, as in the fulfilment of one's obligations

explanation.definitionFit: A weapon is let off when fired, and duties are carried out or fulfilled; one word covers both senses.

clue.text: One of the seven, faces of London

definitions.text: One of the seven, faces of London

parts.words: One of the seven, faces of London
parts.note: A slang word for a face, and a clock face

explanation.walkthrough: Seven Dials is a junction in London's West End named after a pillar with sundials; 'dial' is also slang for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock face, and slang for a person's face, is the same word as the one in Seven Dials, a London junction.

clue.text: A god has other things besides merry making in Rome

parts.note: Saturn is the Roman god of agriculture
alia is Latin for other things

explanation.surface: A Roman god enjoys various extras on top of a party in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin piece fits the Roman setting: alia means 'other things'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman festival of December was a time of feasting and revelry, so it is Roman merrymaking.

clue.text: Potential brick-dropper

parts.note: dropping a brick is British slang for a social blunder, but a labourer carrying bricks in a hod might literally drop one

explanation.walkthrough: To 'drop a brick' is British slang for a tactless remark; here the bricks are real ones a labourer carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder's labourer carries bricks in a trough on the shoulder and so could literally let one fall.

clue.text: It's distasteful to turn up in anger for the start

annotationWithheld.why: It's distasteful to turn up in anger for the start (9): no parse found; turn up gives PU, leaving REGNANT, which 'in anger for the start' does not give with any indicator I can account for
annotationWithheld.clue: It's distasteful to turn up in anger for the start

clue.text: Trainee priest hoped to change into one

definitions.text: Trainee priest hoped to change into one

indicators.note: to change says the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: fodder as written

explanation.surface: A novice priest hopes to be ordained one day.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: this is a Jewish priestly vestment a trainee priest might put on. 'Change into' reads as becoming, but it is also changing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The ephod was the linen apron worn by ancient Hebrew priests, a garment one would change into.

clue.text: Concerning a potentate, sort of square yet consequential.

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
a sultan is a Muslim ruler, a potentate
a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler, so T is a sort of square

explanation.surface: A description of some ruler as being both upright in character and important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a description of the potentate's character, but it points to the T-square, giving just T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something following as a result of an earlier cause is consequential, an outcome.

clue.text: Takes charge in anti-submarine campaign

parts.note: the charge here is the explosive dropped from a ship to destroy submarines, named after the sea measurement that sets it off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes charge' reads as assuming command, but it means the word that goes with 'charge' in an anti-submarine weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A depth charge is the anti-submarine bomb; the word that precedes 'charge' in its name is the measurement of how far down.

clue.text: Non-swimmer at the end of the line

definitions.text: Non-swimmer at the end of the line

parts.words: Non-swimmer at the end of the line
parts.note: an angler's weight that goes straight to the bottom, hanging at the tip of the fishing line

explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end of the line' sounds like a person in despair, but the line is a fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing weight on the end of the line is something that goes under rather than floating, a non-swimmer.

clue.text: Fixed the place for shooting in a road

indicators.note: in says the shooting place sits inside the abbreviation for road

parts.note: a firing range is a place for shooting practice

explanation.surface: Someone describes a shooting gallery being set up beside a highway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fixed or settled in advance has been organised, as with a meeting set up beforehand.

clue.text: Envelope left behind by an astronaut

definitions.text: Envelope left behind by an astronaut

parts.words: Envelope left behind by an astronaut
parts.note: the layer of gases around the Earth, which a rocket passes through and leaves behind on reaching space

explanation.walkthrough: 'Envelope' suggests a letter left behind, but it is the layer of air around the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The air surrounding the planet is its gaseous envelope, which a space traveller leaves once beyond it.

clue.text: Short and clear for a change, this music

indicators.note: for a change says these letters are to be altered into a different order

parts.note: fodder as written
fodder as written

explanation.surface: A request that some music be made brief and lucid for once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short and clear for a change' reads as wanting brevity, but 'for a change' shuffles the ten letters of SHORT and CLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Music written for a full symphony band of strings, brass and woodwind is described this way.

clue.text: As numerous as the next hatching?

definitions.text: As numerous as the next hatching?

parts.words: As numerous as the next hatching?
parts.note: the proverb says not to number your chickens before they hatch, so the coming brood must stay unnumbered

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'Don't count your chickens before they're hatched'.
explanation.definitionFit: Innumerable things are too many to tally, and the proverb forbids tallying chicks before they hatch.

clue.text: Dynasty of taste

definitions.meaning: the ruling house of China from 618 to 907

explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese imperial house of the seventh to tenth centuries shares its name with a sharp flavour, as of citrus.

clue.text: Root for an orphan of the storm?

definitions.text: Root for an orphan of the storm?

parts.words: Root for an orphan of the storm?
parts.note: a lost girl in a gale is a gal in a gale, and the run of those words names an aromatic root

explanation.walkthrough: 'Root for' reads as cheering on the orphan, but 'Root' is the definition and the rest pictures a gal in a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: The ginger-like aromatic rootstock used in Asian cooking is this plant; its name reads as a girl caught in a gale.

clue.text: With eyes they see not, in Runyopese currency

definitions.meaning: tubers have buds called eyes, which cannot see
in Damon Runyon's stories of New York gangsters, dollars are called by this vegetable's name

explanation.walkthrough: Damon Runyon was an American writer whose gangster characters speak a slangy dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: The tubers have sprouting buds called eyes, and Damon Runyon's Broadway characters use the vegetable's name as slang for dollars.

clue.text: A case for some private tuition

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A school offering an example of one-to-one coaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a legal or study case for the tutor, but it is a small container.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental holder for needles and sewing items is this kind of case.

clue.text: The hold for a TV wrestler pinning down his opponent?

definitions.text: The hold for a TV wrestler pinning down his opponent?

parts.words: The hold for a TV wrestler pinning down his opponent?
parts.note: old television sets had a control keeping the picture steady side to side; a wrestler pinning a rival keeps them lying flat

explanation.walkthrough: Old TV sets had a 'hold' knob for the picture's level; the clue blends that with a wrestling hold that leaves the opponent lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: The television control for the picture's side-to-side stability is named after lying flat, as a pinned wrestler does.

clue.text: A design for all to make

indicators.note: to make says the letters are fashioned into a new word

parts.note: fodder as written
fodder as written

explanation.surface: A pattern that anyone can create for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern of flowers is a common decorative design on fabrics and wallpaper.

clue.text: Note leap, when disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: fodder as written
fodder as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to observe how something jumps when startled.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: this grazing animal bounds away when startled, and NOTE LEAP rearranged spells it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazelles and springbok are grazing animals famous for bounding away when alarmed.

clue.text: One of many (associated with) snakes-dicey!

parts.note: a common European viper is one of many snakes, and in the dice game of snakes and ... a player who totals throws is one who sums

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hints at the board game snakes and ladders, where dice are thrown and snakes send you down.
explanation.definitionFit: The common viper is a snake, and a person who totals figures sums them; the snakes-and-ladders board joins the two.

clue.text: River study by Merlin for example

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: The wizard Merlin is pictured studying beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Merlin suggests the Arthurian wizard, but a merlin is also a small hawk. The Fal is a river in Cornwall, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The merlin is a small bird of prey, one of the hawk family, so it is an example of this raptor.

clue.text: Willow structure at Olivia's gate

parts.note: in Twelfth Night, Viola says she would make a willow hut at Olivia's gate and call upon her

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Twelfth Night, Act 1 Scene 5, where Viola describes wooing Olivia.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola's speech in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night begins 'Make me a willow cabin at your gate', a small hut.

clue.text: Detect a thing of beauty

definitions.meaning: to notice or catch sight of
a beauty ... is a small dark mark on the face, or a scenic place

explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to see it, and a beauty mark or a lovely view is a beauty one of these.

clue.text: Would it be so dismal get ting the old penny back?

parts.note: d was the abbreviation for a penny in British money before 1971
the rear is the back part

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether recovering an old coin would be gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: In pre-decimal British money d stood for a penny (from Latin denarius).
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic word for gloomy and depressing.

clue.text: Plant causes sense, of well-being round Beachy. Head

indicators.note: round says the feeling goes around the letter taken from the next word

parts.note: euphoria is an intense feeling of happiness

indicators.note: head says take the first letter of Beachy

explanation.surface: A plant is said to bring a happy mood near Beachy Head, the famous Sussex cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: Beachy Head is a chalk headland on England's south coast, but here 'Head' just takes B, the first letter of Beachy.
explanation.definitionFit: The spurges are a large genus of plants with milky sap, of which poinsettia is an example.

clue.text: Like a bouncer, putting one right in the balance

indicators.note: in says the two pieces go inside the word for the balance

parts.note: the rest is what remains, the balance
I is the Roman numeral one
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman is said to be adding a correct figure to the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman, but here it is a bouncing thing, like a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball that springs back into shape and rebounds has elasticity, so this describes something bouncy.

clue.text: Exotic monkey in a barber's shop

definitions.meaning: French, a foreign language, has this word for a monkey
barbers once offered to burn off split hair ends with a taper

explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic' here means foreign: this is the French word for monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: French for monkey is this word, and a light burning of hair ends was a traditional barber's treatment.
